# Zauberer Lua API

Package scripts run in a sandbox (no `io`, `os`, `dofile`, `loadfile` or binary chunks). Every package has its own environment; `require` loads modules from the package overlay. Functions marked *Test API* exist only in Lua tests (`--test`) and scenarios (`--scenario`).

## engine: lifecycle, time and state

### `engine.api_version: string`

The scripting API version packages declare in package.lua ("api").

### `engine.version: string`

The engine version.

### `engine.credits(): Credit[]`

Asset credits of every loaded package (credits.lua) and the third-party code notices.

### `engine.hash_state(value?: any): string`

Canonical 64-bit state hash as 16 hex digits. Without an argument: tick, input, random-number counter and every package's "hash" hook; with a value: the same base extended by that value (sorted keys, exact numbers).

### `engine.info(): EngineInfo`

Engine version, scripting API, platform, build, input mode, drawable size and seed.

### `engine.log(level: "debug"|"info"|"warn"|"error", message: string)`

Writes a message to the engine log.

### `engine.on(event: "init"|"tick"|"frame"|"event"|"shutdown"|"reload"|"hash", fn: function)`

Registers a lifecycle hook of the calling package: tick(dt), frame(alpha), event(name, args), reload(preserved) and hash() (returns the package's simulation state for replays). A hook that raises an error is disabled.

### `engine.packages(): PackageInfo[]`

Enabled packages in load order, then disabled ones with the reason.

### `engine.pause(paused: boolean)`

Pauses or resumes the simulation; frames and frame hooks continue while paused.

### `engine.preserve(state: table)`

Development builds: keeps state across hot reloads; it is passed to the package's reload hook.

### `engine.quit(code?: integer)`

Ends the game after this tick; shutdown hooks run in reverse load order. The process exits with code (default 0).

### `engine.reset(keep?: string[]): boolean, string?`

Starts the game over as at its first start, after this tick: every saved game is deleted, the save data keeps only the keys named in keep (the player's settings, say), and the scripts, the world and the simulation are made anew. The configuration (bindings, packages) is kept. False with a reason when it cannot be: in a co-op session, in tests and scenarios.

### `engine.resize_window(width: integer, height: integer)`

Test API (scenarios and Lua tests only): resizes the window.

### `engine.set_flash_strength(strength: number)`

How bright flashes of light such as lightning are drawn, 0 .. 1 (default 1; reduced flashing turns it down).

### `engine.set_fullscreen(on: boolean)`

Switches the window to fullscreen or back; scripts receive a resize event.

### `engine.set_package_enabled(id: string, on: boolean): boolean, string?`

Turns a package (a mod) on or off from the next start; the choice is kept with the player's settings. The base game cannot be turned off. Returns false and the reason when the change cannot be made.

### `engine.set_time_scale(scale: number)`

Development and test builds only: simulation speed factor (0.1 to 10).

### `engine.tick(): integer`

Number of simulation ticks run so far.

### `engine.time(): number`

Simulation time in seconds (ticks / 60). Use it instead of wall-clock time.

## vfs: package files

### `vfs.exists(path: string): boolean`

Whether a file exists in the merged package view.

### `vfs.list(dir?: string): DirEntry[]?, string?`

Merged listing of a directory across packages.

### `vfs.load(path: string, callback: fun(data: string?, err: string?)): "pending"`

Loads a file asynchronously; callback runs in a later frame.

### `vfs.read(path: string): string?, string?`

Reads a file synchronously through the overlay; returns nil and an error message on failure. Prefer vfs.load for large files.

## input: actions and bindings

### `input.add_button(name: string, x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number)`

Adds an on-screen button for "touch:button:<name>" bindings.

### `input.add_stick(name: string, x: number, y: number, radius: number)`

Adds an on-screen stick (normalised screen coordinates) for "touch:stick:<name>" bindings.

### `input.bind(action: string, binding: string)`

Adds a binding such as "key:space", "keys:w,s,a,d", "mouse:left", "gamepad:left_stick", "touch:button:spin", "xr:select" or "xr:right_squeeze" (WebXR controllers; "xr:select" and "xr:squeeze" accept either hand).

### `input.bindings(action: string): string[]`

Current bindings of an action.

### `input.capture(): string?`

The binding ("key:x", "mouse:left", "gamepad:a") of the last key or button pressed since the previous call, for remapping controls (pass it to input.set_user_binding); nil when nothing was pressed.

### `input.clear(action: string)`

Removes all bindings of an action.

### `input.define(name: string, kind?: "button"|"axis1"|"axis2"): integer`

Defines an action (or returns the existing one of the same kind).

### `input.inject(action: string, x?: number, y?: number, ticks?: integer)`

Test API: overrides an action's value for the next ticks (default 1, 0, 1).

### `input.mode(): "desktop"|"touch"`

The current input mode.

### `input.set_user_binding(action: string, bindings: string[]): boolean`

Replaces the player's bindings of an action and saves the configuration; returns whether saving succeeded.

### `input.state(action: string): ActionState`

The action's snapshot for this tick.

## render: models, sprites, text and camera

### `render.atmosphere(atmosphere: Atmosphere|false)`

Sky and fog. The engine keeps the horizon's up direction and dip in step with the camera over the planet. false switches both off.

### `render.camera(camera: Camera)`

Sets the camera for the following frames.

### `render.capture(target?: "internal"|"window"): { width: integer, height: integer }?, string?`

Test API: reads back the last frame.

### `render.clear_color(r: number, g: number, b: number)`

Background colour.

### `render.daylight(on: boolean)`

Lights the scene from the world's sky (the sun, the moon and the stars, day and night, the seasons of plants and snow) instead of render.light and the colours of render.atmosphere; its fog distance still applies.

### `render.draw_model(model: integer, transform?: Transform)`

Draws a model this frame (call from a frame hook).

### `render.draw_sprite(sprite: integer, position: number[], scale?: number, time?: number)`

Draws a camera-facing sprite; the animation frame follows time (default: the pinned render time if pinned, else simulation time).

### `render.draw_text(font: integer, text: string, x: number, y: number, scale?: number, color?: number[])`

Draws UTF-8 text in internal pixels (origin top-left); missing characters use the replacement glyph.

### `render.font(path: string): integer`

Starts loading a bitmap-font descriptor.

### `render.internal_height(height?: integer): integer`

Gets or sets the internal rendering height (default 360).

### `render.light(light: Light)`

Sets the directional light and ambient term.

### `render.match_golden(name: string, target?: "internal"|"window"): boolean, string`

Test API: compares the frame with tests/golden/<name>.png (channel delta <= 8, <= 0.5 % pixels); ZB_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 creates missing images.

### `render.model(path: string): integer`

Starts loading a glTF model (.glb/.gltf); returns its handle.

### `render.palette(palette: Palette|false)`

Quantises the scene to the palette with ordered dithering (text stays as drawn); false switches it off.

### `render.pin_time(seconds?: number)`

Holds the time that animates water and swaying plants (for photos and golden images); nil lets it run with the game again.

### `render.pixel(x: integer, y: integer): integer, integer, integer, integer`

Test API: RGBA of a pixel of the last capture (origin top-left).

### `render.sprite(path: string): integer`

Starts loading a sprite descriptor (texture, frame size, frames, fps, pivot, size).

### `render.sprite_frame(sprite: integer, time: number): integer`

Number of animation frames the sprite has advanced at time.

### `render.state(handle: integer): "pending"|"ready"|"failed"`

Loading state of an asset; failed assets draw placeholders.

### `render.stats(): RenderStats`

Layout and draw statistics of the last frame.

### `render.text_glyphs(font: integer, text: string): integer[]`

Glyph indices the font uses for text.

### `render.texture(path: string): integer`

Starts loading a PNG texture; returns its handle.

### `render.vignette(strength: number|false): number`

Comfort vignette: darkens the edges of every view (around each eye's optical centre in VR) by up to strength (0 .. 1; 0 or false switches it off), e.g. while the carpet turns or speeds up. Returns the strength in effect.

### `render.xr_hud(distance: number|false, pixel?: number): number`

Screen text in VR is drawn at the headset's resolution. false or 0 (the default) shows the canvas (one view's width, render.stats().internal_width / views, by the internal height) filling every eye's view; a distance (metres, up to 1000) puts it on a plane that far in front of the head instead, the canvas centre straight ahead, so both eyes see it in the same direction. pixel is the size of a canvas pixel on that plane in metres (default: as wide as a pixel in the middle of the view). Returns the distance in effect.

### `audio.decoder_bytes(voice: integer): integer`

Decoder memory of a streaming voice.

### `audio.group_volume(group: "master"|"music"|"effects", volume?: number): number?`

Gets or sets a volume group (setting "master" returns nothing).

### `audio.locked(): boolean`

Web: true until the first user gesture allows audio.

### `audio.play(path: string, options?: PlayOptions): integer`

Plays a WAV or OGG file; returns a voice handle (0 when all voices are busy).

### `audio.set_volume(voice: integer, volume: number)`

### `audio.state(voice: integer): "playing"|"stopped"`

Whether a voice still plays.

### `audio.stop(voice: integer)`

Stops a voice.

### `audio.voices(): integer`

Number of active voices.

## save: player data

### `save.flush(): boolean`

Writes the save data to the user data directory.

### `save.get(key: string): any`

Reads a value from the player's save data.

### `save.set(key: string, value: nil|boolean|number|string|table)`

## world: planet coordinates and terrain

### `world.biome(pos: PlanetPos): string?`

The biome under a position, nil in the noise world.

### `world.chunk_hash(pos: PlanetPos, stage?: integer): string`

Generates the position's chunk to a stage (default 1) and returns the hash of its data as 16 hex digits: peers compare it to check that they generate the same world.

### `world.chunk_key(pos: PlanetPos): integer`

The chunk's stable 64-bit key.

### `world.chunk_stage(pos: PlanetPos): integer`

Stage the position's chunk is loaded at (0 coarse, 1 heightfield, 2 surface, 3 plants), or -1.

### `world.clear_focus(index: integer)`

Removes a focus point; its chunks are released as memory requires.

### `world.climate(pos: PlanetPos, month?: integer): number?, number?`

Mean temperature (C, at the position's altitude) and precipitation (mm) for a month (1-12), or the year when month is omitted; nil in the noise world.

### `world.create(options?: WorldOptions): boolean, string?`

Starts creating a new world (one at a time); world.create_step does the work.

### `world.create_cancel()`

Abandons the world being created.

### `world.create_finish(name: string): boolean, string?`

Saves the finished world as worlds/<name>.zbw in the user folder and makes it the world being played. Names use letters, digits, - and _.

### `world.create_step(pieces?: integer): CreationProgress?`

Does some pieces of work (default 1: a deep-time step, an erosion pass, a month of climate); nil when no world is being created.

### `world.cut_plant(id: integer): boolean`

Cuts a plant (its id from world.plants): felled, dug up or picked whole, it is gone until it has grown back (ground cover in weeks, shrubs in months, trees in years); the edit is kept with the world. False when the plant is not loaded or already gone.

### `world.deform(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number, amount: number): integer`

Digs (amount < 0) or raises the ground within radius metres (0.5 .. 64) of a place by up to amount metres (-30 .. 30) at the centre, in a smooth bowl or mound: a crater, an Earth spell. Plants inside are dug up, the change is kept with the game, and the active tier's water and fire follow the new ground. Returns the chunks changed (0 where the ground is not loaded).

### `world.distance(a: PlanetPos, b: PlanetPos): number`

Great-circle distance at sea level in metres.

### `world.draw_globe(frame: integer?, position: number[], radius: number, spin?: number): boolean`

Draws the planet as a globe: a time-lapse frame of the world being created (1-based; nil for the newest), or the played world by biome when none is being created. Returns false when there is nothing to show yet.

### `world.export_bundle(): string?`

The created world being played as bytes (its bundle), to send to heirs joining a co-op session; nil in the noise world.

### `world.find_water(pos: PlanetPos, kind: "river"|"lake"|"ocean", radius: number?): PlanetPos?`

The nearest place within radius metres (default 50 km) where a created world has water of a kind: for a river, the middle of the channel leaving the nearest macro cell that has one; for a lake or the sea, the centre of the nearest such cell. nil in the noise world or when there is none.

### `world.flora(): Species[]`

The plant species of the world, in registry order.

### `world.from_cartesian(x: number, y: number, z: number): PlanetPos`

The position of planet-centred coordinates in metres.

### `world.from_local(x: number, y: number, z: number): PlanetPos`

The position at render coordinates.

### `world.ground_height(pos: PlanetPos): number`

Ground height in metres above sea level from the loaded heightfield (the analytic terrain where the chunk is not loaded at stage 1 or more).

### `world.ground_surface(pos: PlanetPos): string?`

The surface material of the 1 m cell at a position from its loaded chunk (stage 2 or more, with the players' edits), or nil when it is not loaded.

### `world.height(pos: PlanetPos): number`

Terrain height above sea level in metres at the position (the analytic terrain, within 0.5 m of the generated heightfield).

### `world.info(): WorldInfo`

The world being played.

### `world.load(name: string): boolean, string?`

Plays in the created world <name> from the user folder (saves/<name>/, or worlds/<name>.zbw from before saves).

### `world.load_game(name: string): table|boolean|nil, string?`

Plays the saved world <name> again: its world, time and the players' edits. Returns the player table it was saved with (true if there was none), or nil and a message. Created worlds from before saves (worlds/<name>.zbw) are moved into saves/<name>/.

### `world.minerals(pos: PlanetPos): string[]?`

The mineral deposits under a position, nil in the noise world.

### `world.move(pos: PlanetPos, heading: number, forward: number, right?: number, up?: number): PlanetPos, number`

Moves a position forward metres along heading (radians clockwise from north), right metres to the side and up metres up; returns the new position and the heading carried along the path (straight flight follows a great circle, also across the poles).

### `world.neighbors(pos: PlanetPos): PlanetPos[]`

Centres of the chunks sharing an edge or corner with the position's chunk (7 or 8).

### `world.planet(): PlanetInfo`

Describes the planet.

### `world.plants(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number): Plant[]`

The plants within radius metres (up to 256) of a position, from the chunks loaded with their plants (stage 3); at most 4096.

### `world.play_bundle(data: string): boolean, string?`

Plays in a created world given as bytes (a bundle a co-op host sent); nil and why when they are not a world bundle.

### `world.position(face: integer, x: integer, y: integer, lx?: number, ly?: number, alt?: number): PlanetPos`

Makes a position; the offsets default to 0. Errors when the chunk is not on the planet.

### `world.province(pos: PlanetPos): integer?, number?`

The biogeographic province under a position (1-based) and its isolation (0 well connected .. 1 remote), nil at sea or in the noise world.

### `world.remove_plants(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number): integer`

Removes the plants within radius metres (up to 256) of a position from the loaded chunks; the edit is kept with the world (and saved). Returns how many.

### `world.save_game(name: string, player?: table): boolean, string?`

Saves the world being played under saves/<name>/: its time, the players' edits and a player table (literal values only) for the scripts.

### `world.saves(): string[]`

The names of the saved games in the user folder, sorted.

### `world.set_focus(index: integer, pos: PlanetPos, velocity?: number[], view?: number[])`

Streams terrain around a focus point (1..4, one per player camera). velocity (m/s) and view are {x, y, z} in the local frame at pos (x east, y up, z south).

### `world.set_surface(pos: PlanetPos, material: string)`

Sets the surface material ("soil", "sand", "rock", "gravel", "snow", "ice", "mud") of the 1 m cell at a position; the edit is kept with the world.

### `world.set_time(seconds: number)`

Sets the world's time (game seconds since the world began), e.g. after sleeping.

### `world.sky(pos: PlanetPos): Sky`

The sky over a position now.

### `world.strata(pos: PlanetPos): Stratum[]?`

The rock record under a position, youngest first, nil in the noise world.

### `world.stream_stats(): StreamStats`

Chunk streaming statistics.

### `world.surface(pos: PlanetPos): string`

Surface material at the position: "soil", "sand", "rock", "gravel", "snow", "ice" or "mud".

### `world.time(): WorldTime`

The world's time and date (the clock at longitude 0).

### `world.to_cartesian(pos: PlanetPos): number, number, number`

Planet-centred coordinates in metres (+Z is the north pole).

### `world.to_local(pos: PlanetPos): number[]`

Render coordinates {x, y, z} of a position (relative to the floating origin; x east, y up, z south at the origin).

### `world.up_at(pos: PlanetPos): number[]`

The local up direction at a position, in render coordinates (it tilts with the planet's curvature away from the origin).

### `world.view_distance(near?: number, far?: number): number, number`

Gets or sets the streaming rings: chunks get full detail within near metres and coarse detail within far metres (growing with altitude up to twice far).

### `world.water(pos: PlanetPos): string?, number?, number?, number?, number?`

Water at a position: its kind ("ocean", "lake" or "river"; nil on dry land), the water surface in metres above sea level, its depth, and the current towards east and north in m/s.

### `world.weather(pos: PlanetPos): NaturalWeather`

The world's own weather at a place now (what the sky does there, whatever the scripts set for the simulations).

## net: co-op sessions

### `net.blob_cached(hash: string): boolean`

True when the blob cache in the user directory holds this hash (so a join can skip the transfer).

### `net.blob_hash(data: string): string`

The content hash used for blobs and the cache (SHA-1 as 40 hex digits).

### `net.blob_load(hash: string): string?`

A cached blob, checked against its hash, or nil (a damaged file is removed).

### `net.blob_store(data: string): string?, string?`

Stores a blob in the cache in the user directory; returns its hash, or nil and why it failed.

### `net.host(port?: integer): integer?, string?`

Hosts a co-op session (desktop only); returns the port in use (port 0 or omitted picks a free one), or nil and why it failed.

### `net.host_relay(url: string): boolean, string?`

Hosts a co-op session through a relay at a ws:// address (also in the browser); once the relay answers, net.status().invite_code holds the code to give to friends. If the relay refuses or is lost, net.receive reports "ended" with the reason.

### `net.join(url: string): boolean, string?`

Starts joining the session at a ws:// address; net.receive reports "welcome" or "ended".

### `net.join_code(url: string, code: string): boolean, string?`

Starts joining the session with an invite code through the relay at a ws:// address (case, spaces and dashes in the code do not matter); net.receive reports "welcome" or "ended" (with the relay's reason for unknown or expired codes and full sessions).

### `net.lan_announce(on: boolean, name?: string, port?: integer): boolean, string?`

Answers LAN discovery queries while hosting (desktop only; in the browser it fails with "unavailable"), with the session's name and the port to join on (default: the port of the last net.host). net.lan_announce(false) stops.

### `net.lan_scan(): LanSession[]?, string?`

Sessions announced on the local network (desktop only; in the browser nil and "unavailable"). Each call collects answers and asks again once a second, so the first call usually returns an empty list: call it every frame or so while showing the list. Sessions not heard from for three seconds drop out.

### `net.leave()`

Leaves the session (a host ends it for everyone).

### `net.receive(): NetMessage[]`

Messages and session events since the last call, in arrival order.

### `net.rejoin(): boolean, string?`

After the connection to the host was lost (net.status().can_rejoin), connects again the same way (address or invite code); within the host's grace period (30 s) this game gets its player index back. net.receive reports "welcome" or "ended" as for a join.

### `net.send(channel: string, value: any, to?: integer): boolean, string?`

Sends a value (nil, booleans, numbers, strings and tables of them) on a channel to a player, or to everyone when to is omitted (clients' messages travel through the host).

### `net.send_blob(to: integer, name: string, data: string): boolean, string?`

Sends a large blob (such as the world bundle) to one player (clients: only to the host, 0) in flow-controlled chunks that do not hold up the channels; the receiver gets "blob_progress" events and then "blob" once the content hash matches, the sender "blob_sent" or "blob_failed".

### `net.set_budget(kbps: integer, burst_kbps?: integer)`

Sets the bandwidth budget per connection (default 64 kbit/s on average with bursts of up to 256 kbit/s for a second). Reliable messages count against it but are always sent.

### `net.set_channel(channel: string, class: string): boolean, string?`

Sets how a channel travels (the same on every player): "reliable" (the default: every message arrives) or "latest" (while a connection is over its bandwidth budget only the newest unsent message per channel and sender is kept; for snapshots and positions).

### `net.status(): NetStatus`

The session's state.

## xr: WebXR session and head tracking

### `xr.emulate(head?: XrPose|false)`

Test API: starts or moves an emulated headset at the head pose (default: the session origin). Its two views render side by side into the window, eyes 64 mm apart, through the same path as a real session. false ends the session.

### `xr.emulate_button(hand: "left"|"right"|"none", button: "select"|"squeeze", down: boolean)`

Test API: a controller button event, as a headset reports it ("none" for sources without a hand).

### `xr.emulate_controller(hand: "left"|"right", pose: XrPose|false, axes?: number[], trigger?: number, squeeze?: number)`

Test API: the emulated headset's controller of a hand from now on, as xr.state().controllers reports it: tracked at the pose (relative to the session origin), or untracked for false; the thumbstick {x, y} (default {0, 0}, each -1 .. 1), the trigger and the squeeze (default 0, each 0 .. 1).

### `xr.state(): XrState`

The WebXR session. While it runs, the camera set with render.camera is the session origin (the seat on the carpet): every eye sees the scene from the head pose relative to it, with the headset's field of view. The head pose is updated before the frame hooks of every XR frame; it is presentation data and not part of replays. The controllers (poses, thumbsticks, trigger and squeeze of the left and right hands) are updated with it and are presentation data in the same way. A session start or end reaches the event hook as "xr_session" (value "started" or "ended"); controller buttons are bindings such as "xr:select" (see input.bind).

## test: Lua tests

### `test.case(name: string, fn: function)`

Lua tests (--test): registers a test case.

### `test.expect(value: any, message?: string): boolean`

Fails unless value is truthy. Also available as expect() in scenarios, where failures are counted and the scenario continues.

### `test.expect_eq(actual: any, expected: any, message?: string): boolean`

Fails unless actual == expected. Also expect_eq() in scenarios.

### `test.expect_error(fn: function, substring?: string): boolean`

Fails unless fn raises an error (containing substring). Also expect_error() in scenarios.

### `test.expect_near(actual: number, expected: number, eps?: number, message?: string): boolean`

Fails unless |actual - expected| <= eps (default 1e-6). Also expect_near() in scenarios.

## math: deterministic randomness

### `math.random(m?: integer, n?: integer): number`

Deterministic random numbers from the run's seed.

### `math.randomseed(seed?: integer)`

Restarts the random sequence (default: the run's seed).

## Globals

### `package_id: string`

Id of the package whose script is running (package environments only).

### `load(chunk: string, name?: string, mode?: string, env?: table): function?, string?`

Compiles Lua source text; binary chunks are always rejected.

### `print(...: any)`

Writes the values to the engine log.

### `require(name: string): any`

Loads scripts/<name with dots as slashes>.lua through the package overlay, once.

### `scenario(info: { name: string })`

Scenarios (--scenario): names the scenario in reports.

### `sleep(ms: integer)`

Scenarios: waits ms milliseconds of real time (for tests with several processes; the web build does not block).

### `step(ticks?: integer)`

Scenarios: runs ticks simulation ticks (default 1) before continuing.

## gesture

### `gesture.forms(): string[]`

The eight forms: tap, line, circle, spiral, triangle, square, zigzag, wave.

### `gesture.recognize(points: number[], options?: GestureOptions): Gesture`

Recognises a stroke given as { x1, y1, x2, y2, ... } (up to 4096 points), in any orientation, drawn either way round. Strokes shorter than tap_size are taps.

### `gesture.template(form: string, count?: integer): number[]`

The stroke of a form at unit size as { x1, y1, ... } with count points (default 32, 2 .. 512): for tracing guides and tests.

## mana

### `mana.at(pos: PlanetPos): ManaCell`

The mana of the 32 m cell at a place in the active tier.

### `mana.colors(): string[]`

The eight colours in the order of the mana wheel: fire, storm, light, life, water, earth, void, decay (opposites are four apart).

### `mana.draw(pos: PlanetPos, color: string, amount: number, radius?: number): number`

Draws up to amount mana (0 .. 1e6) of a colour from the cells within radius metres (default 0: the cell at pos; up to 256); returns how much it got. Emptying a cell with heavy drawing blights it.

### `mana.ley(pos: PlanetPos): LeySample`

The ley network near a place (anywhere on the planet).

### `mana.release(pos: PlanetPos, color: string, amount: number)`

Gives mana back to the field at a place (0 .. 1e6): motes dissolving, spells fading.

### `mana.set_ley_strength(strength: number): number`

Sets the ley network's strength (0 .. 1; the story weakens or restores it) and returns the strength before. Mana flows from lines and nexuses in proportion.

### `mana.stats(): ManaStats`



## registry

### `registry.get(kind: string, ref: string): RegistryEntry?`

An entry as its packages left it: its fields, plus key, package (that added it) and changed (the last package that overrode or patched it). ref is a key or an id that only one package defines; nil when there is no such entry.

### `registry.keys(kind: string): string[]`

The keys ("package:id") of a registry's entries in load order. Kinds: "materials".

## sim

### `sim.add_fuel(pos: PlanetPos, kg: number, radius?: number): integer`

Lays kg (0 .. 1000) of dry wood within radius metres (default 0.5, up to 8) of a place: a campfire to light. Returns the cells that took it (none under water or burning).

### `sim.add_heat(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number, joules: number)`

Adds heat spread over radius metres (up to 64): enough of it dries and then ignites the fuel there.

### `sim.add_water(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number, cubic_metres: number): integer`

Pours water over the ground within radius metres (up to 64) of a place in the active tier: a spell, a spring, a broken dam. Returns the cells (about 2 m) that got some; the sea, lakes and rivers take none.

### `sim.air_stats(): AirStats`

The air of the active tier.

### `sim.bodies_near(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number): integer[]`

Ids of the bodies whose centre is within radius metres (up to 256).

### `sim.body(id: integer): Body?`

A body as it is now, or nil when there is no such body.

### `sim.body_stats(): BodyStats`



### `sim.bond(id: integer, metres: number|nil): boolean`

Binds a creature to the player (summoned, a familiar): it follows, keeping within metres (0.5 .. 50) of the player, and neither fears nor hunts the player; nil lets it go. False when there is no such creature.

### `sim.cool(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number, joules: number): integer`

Takes heat from within radius metres (up to 64): a heat sink, magic unmaking fire. Burning cells that lose more than 50 kJ/m^2 go out; returns how many did.

### `sim.creature(id: integer): Creature?`

A creature as it is now, or nil.

### `sim.creature_events(): CreatureEvent[]`

What happened to creatures since last asked.

### `sim.creature_stats(): CreatureStats`



### `sim.creatures_near(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number): integer[]`

Ids of the creatures within radius metres (up to 256), the dead included.

### `sim.define_species(species: Species): integer`

Defines a creature species (a later definition of the same id replaces it); returns its index. Errors for values out of range or too many species.

### `sim.emit(pos: PlanetPos, gas: string, kg: number)`

Releases kg of a gas ("smoke", "steam", "scent" or "fumes") into the air above a place in the active tier: a creature's scent, a potion's fumes.

### `sim.fire_at(pos: PlanetPos): FireCell`

The 2 m cell of the heat and fire simulation at a place.

### `sim.fire_stats(): FireStats`

The heat and fire simulation as a whole.

### `sim.freeze(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number, seconds: number): integer`

Freezes the water within radius metres (up to 64), standing water and the sea, lakes and rivers alike, for seconds (0 .. 86400) of simulated time: ice that does not flow and can be walked on. Returns the cells frozen.

### `sim.gas_at(pos: PlanetPos): Gases`

The gases in the air at a place, kg/m^3 of the lowest air layer.

### `sim.hurt(id: integer, harm: string, amount: number): boolean`

Hurts a creature (amount > 0, less its resistance to the harm) or heals it (amount < 0); returns whether it lives.

### `sim.ignite(pos: PlanetPos, radius?: number): integer`

Sets fire to the fuel within radius metres (default 2, up to 64) of a place in the active tier: lightning, a spell, a torch. Returns the cells (about 2 m) that caught; wet or bare ground and water do not.

### `sim.launch(pos: PlanetPos, velocity: Vector, radius?: number, mass?: number): integer`

Throws a projectile (a stone, an arrow, a bolt of magic) from pos: a small sphere of radius metres (default 0.05, up to 0.5) and mass kg (default 0.5, up to 100) under gravity. It never passes through anything; a hit stops it and pushes the body it struck. Returns its id; errors when out of range.

### `sim.lightning(pos: PlanetPos): integer`

Lightning strikes a place in the active tier: a flash, and fire in the dry fuel there. Returns the cells that caught.

### `sim.material(ref: string): Material?`

What the simulations use of a material (SI units, deg C); nil when there is no such material.

### `sim.material_at(ref: string, temperature: number): string`

The material ref becomes at a temperature (deg C) through its phase changes: water at -5 is ice, ice at 150 is steam. Errors for an unknown material.

### `sim.natural_weather()`

Returns to the world's own weather (from the next second).

### `sim.projectile(id: integer): Projectile?`

A projectile in flight or stopped in the last 10 seconds, else nil.

### `sim.push(id: integer, impulse: Vector): boolean`

Gives a body a push at its centre (N s { east, north, up }) and wakes it; false when there is no such body.

### `sim.remove_body(id: integer): boolean`

Takes a body out of the world; false when there was no such body.

### `sim.remove_creature(id: integer): boolean`

Takes a creature (alive or dead) out of the world.

### `sim.remove_water(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number, cubic_metres: number): number`

Takes up to cubic_metres (0 .. 1e7) of standing water from within radius metres (up to 64): drying magic. Returns how much it took.

### `sim.set_active_radius(metres?: number): number`

The radius (50 .. 2000 m) simulated around each focus point - fire, water, air and mana - so that several areas, one per separated heir, share the host's budget; without an argument only tells it. Returns the radius in use before.

### `sim.set_needs(id: integer, needs: table): boolean`

Sets a creature's needs, each 0 .. 1 and left as it is when omitted: { hunger = .., thirst = .., energy = .. }; it reconsiders what to do at once. Returns whether the creature exists.

### `sim.set_player(pos: PlanetPos|nil, on_foot?: boolean, seen?: PlayerSeen)`

Where the player is for the creatures (nil: nowhere), whether on foot, and how they perceive the player (fields left out are 1).

### `sim.set_weather(weather: Weather)`

Sets the weather the simulations see, instead of the world's own, until sim.natural_weather(): for tests, spells and story moments. Fields left out keep their current values.

### `sim.spare_player(radius: number, seconds: number): integer`

The player is defeated: the hunters within radius metres (up to 500) turn away and leave the player alone for seconds (up to 3600); returns how many.

### `sim.spawn(body: BodyDesc): integer`

Puts a rigid body into the world: a boulder, a log, a crate. It falls, rolls, collides, floats or sinks in the active tier, and waits where it is outside it. Returns its id; errors for a description that does not work (sizes 1 cm .. 50 m, a solid or powder material).

### `sim.spawn_creature(species: string, pos: PlanetPos): integer`

A creature of a species at a place (on the ground, or at its cruising height); returns its id. Errors for an unknown species.

### `sim.stimulus(kind: string, pos: PlanetPos, strength: number, seconds: number)`

Something creatures notice for a while: a "noise" (heard within strength x their hearing), a "light" (seen; in the dark wild animals take it for fire) or a "threat" (feared).

### `sim.sweep(from: PlanetPos, to: PlanetPos, radius?: number): Hit?`

Sweeps a sphere of radius metres (default 0: a ray) from one place to another: the first body or ground it touches, or nil.

### `sim.thaw(pos: PlanetPos, radius: number): integer`

Melts the ice within radius metres (up to 64); returns the cells thawed.

### `sim.tier_stats(): TierStats`

What the active tier costs: milliseconds per tick for each simulation, averaged over the last second, against the budget.

### `sim.water_at(pos: PlanetPos): WaterCell`

The 2 m cell of the surface-water simulation at a place.

### `sim.water_stats(): WaterStats`

Where the water of the active tier is, in m^3: on_ground + soaked + drained + left + removed equals rained + added.

### `sim.weather(): Weather`

The weather the simulations see now, with natural (the world's own, not one the scripts set) and strikes (lightning so far).

### `sim.wind_at(pos: PlanetPos): Wind`

The local wind at a place: the weather's wind shaped by the ground (the weather's wind outside the active tier).

| `reason` | `string?` | Why a blob failed (blob_failed) |
| `error` | `string?` | Why the session ended (ended) |
| `mismatches` | `NetMismatch[]?` | Packages that differed (ended) |

### NetStatus

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `role` | `string` | "none", "host", "joining" or "client" |
| `player` | `integer` | This game's player index (0 = host), -1 when not in a session |
| `players` | `integer[]` | Player indices in the session (players who are away included) |
| `away` | `integer[]` | Players whose connection was lost and who may still come back |
| `error` | `string` | Why the last session ended or failed ("" if it did not) |
| `mismatches` | `NetMismatch[]` | Packages that differed when the host refused the join |
| `can_rejoin` | `boolean` | The connection was lost and net.rejoin may bring this player back |
| `invite_code` | `string?` | The relay's invite code while hosting through a relay |
| `lan` | `boolean` | LAN discovery queries are being answered |
| `rtt_ms` | `integer[]` | Last round trip per player in milliseconds |
| `sent` | `integer` | Bytes sent |
| `received` | `integer` | Bytes received |
| `sent_to` | `integer[]` | Bytes sent to each player (index = player + 1; clients: [1] = the host) |
| `received_from` | `integer[]` | Bytes received from each player |
| `kbps_out` | `integer[]` | kbit/s sent to each player over the last second |
| `kbps_in` | `integer[]` | kbit/s received from each player over the last second |
| `coalesced` | `integer` | Latest-only messages replaced by newer ones before they were sent |
